title: dbpC/contrin (YBX2) normal-tissue and tumor staining, 2006
finding: Normal-tissue staining included vascular smooth muscle and adrenal cortical cells. Specimens included non-tumor surgical regions and autopsies. Reconcile antibody specificity and tissue context before accepting reproductive restriction; the report did not test therapeutic toxicity.

title: ABCC11 axonal localization, Neuroscience 2006
finding: Human brain immunoblotting and axonal immunofluorescence support neural ABCC11 protein. This is a priority conflict with its current retained classification, requiring normal-protein adjudication before target use; clinical injury was not tested.

title: HCA587/MAGEC2 normal and cancer protein staining, 2003
finding: The TC-1 polyclonal reagent stained normal cerebellar Purkinje cells. This priority conflict requires antibody/paralog specificity review; neither the current retained label nor historical staining alone establishes clinical safety or injury.

title: FDA TECELRA label, revised June 2026
finding: Selected synovial sarcoma patients aged 12+: 60/137 responses (43.8%), median response duration 5.3 months. CRS 72% (2% grade >=3), ICANS 4%, grade >=3 infections 12%. Product-specific evidence; not blanket MAGEA4 safety.

title: IMA203 phase 1, Nature Medicine 2025
finding: Confirmed responses: 11/38 (28.9%); unconfirmed-plus-confirmed: 21/40 (52.5%). Severe CRS: 2/41. No severe neurotoxicity or treatment-related deaths reported. This does not establish safety of other PRAME-directed products or rule out rare adrenal injury.

title: Robbins et al., NY-ESO-1 TCR follow-up, 2015
finding: Objective responses in 11/18 synovial sarcomas and 11/20 melanomas. HLA- and antigen-selected, uncontrolled cohort; shared NY-ESO-1 protein attribution does not distinguish CTAG1A from CTAG1B.

title: Robbins et al., NY-ESO-1 TCR follow-up, 2015
finding: Objective responses in 11/18 synovial sarcomas and 11/20 melanomas. HLA- and antigen-selected, uncontrolled cohort; shared NY-ESO-1 protein attribution does not distinguish CTAG1A from CTAG1B.

title: Lete-cel NSCLC pilot studies, 2025
finding: One durable response among 18 treated patients; cytopenias and CRS were common, without fatal treatment-related serious adverse events. Recognition includes a shared NY-ESO-1/LAGE-1A epitope; this is not proof of all-isoform CTAG2 safety.

title: Lete-cel NSCLC pilot studies, 2025
finding: One durable response among 18 treated patients; cytopenias and CRS were common, without fatal treatment-related serious adverse events. Recognition includes a shared NY-ESO-1/LAGE-1A epitope; this is not proof of all-isoform CTAG2 safety.

title: Lete-cel NSCLC pilot studies, 2025

title: Lete-cel myxoid/round-cell liposarcoma pilot, 2025
finding: Responses: 2/10 and 4/10 across two cohorts. A potentially related fatal cardiac arrest occurred on day 161 amid substantial competing illness/treatment. It does not establish CTAG2-mediated myocardial injury; the independent donor-expression hold remains.

title: Linette et al., cardiovascular toxicity and titin cross-reactivity, 2013
finding: Two fatal cardiac events followed affinity-enhanced MAGE-A3 TCR treatment. Cross-recognition of unrelated cardiac titin explains the hazard; it does not demonstrate native MAGEA3 expression in heart.

title: Morgan et al., anti-MAGE-A3 neurological toxicity, 2013
finding: Five of nine patients had tumor regression; three developed neurological toxicity and two died. The receptor cross-recognized MAGE-A12, with brain RNA evidence; pan-MAGE neuronal staining did not uniquely establish the causal paralog.

title: Morgan et al., anti-MAGE-A3 neurological toxicity, 2013

title: MAGRIT randomized phase 3 trial, 2016
finding: MAGE-A3 vaccination did not improve disease-free survival after NSCLC resection (hazard ratio 1.02; 95% CI 0.89-1.18). Trial nomination is therefore not evidence of benefit.

title: ADP-A2M10 NSCLC phase 1, 2022
finding: Eleven treated; one partial response after repeat infusion, followed by aplastic anemia and death. CRS occurred in three patients. Investigators found no evidence of off-target binding or alloreactivity; conditioning and cell-therapy risks remain.

title: ADP-A2M10 head/neck, melanoma and urothelial phase 1, 2022
finding: Ten treated; no objective responses, four stable diseases. Two CRS events resolved. Small cohorts cannot establish absence of rare target-mediated toxicity.

title: BNT211-01 initial phase 1 report, 2023
finding: Initial report: 7/21 unconfirmed responses (33%); CRS 10/22, including one grade 3 event; one grade 1 ICANS. Oncofetal surface-target experience does not validate unrestricted targeting of all developmental tissues.

title: Landscape of immunogenic antigens in successful cervical-cancer TIL therapy, 2017
finding: KK-LC-1 recognition was found in therapeutic TIL associated with complete cervical-cancer regression. Mixed antigen-specific TIL cannot isolate CT83-specific efficacy or safety.

title: CXorf48 as a CML stem-cell immune target, 2017
finding: Human antigen-specific CTLs recognized patient-derived CML stem/progenitor cells. Endogenous immune associations after imatinib cessation support interest, but are not an interventional efficacy or safety trial.

title: FOXR2 is an epigenetically regulated pan-cancer oncogene, 2022
finding: Activation occurred in 8% of individual tumors across 70% of cancer types; experimental work supports ETS-circuit-driven growth. Testis restriction supports reconsideration, but the antibody conflict still needs resolution. No therapeutic outcome is established here.

title: ABCB5 identifies limbal stem cells and supports corneal maintenance, 2014
finding: Normal limbal stem-cell expression and corneal-regeneration function contradict reproductive restriction. Tumor association does not erase the normal eye compartment.

title: Human IL-5-producing T-helper-cell biology, 2012
finding: IL-5 is produced by normal activated immune cells. Baseline tissue silence cannot establish reproductive restriction; neutralizing a secreted cytokine is different from destroying every cell that produces it.

title: Normal human T-cell IL-13 expression, 1996
finding: Activated nonmalignant T cells produce IL-13. State-dependent cytokine expression defeats a reproductive-restricted label even if resting bulk-tissue RNA is low.

title: Regulation of PAPP-A in human coronary vascular cells, 2007
finding: Activated human coronary vascular cells can produce PAPP-A. Placental association does not imply exclusive reproductive expression.

title: SPAG9 in epithelial ovarian cancer, 2007
finding: Ovarian-cancer expression and patient antibody responses establish interest, not reproductive exclusivity. Current normal RNA and protein counterevidence supports exclusion.

title: BAGE antigen recognized by human melanoma-reactive CTLs, 1995
finding: Original human CTL recognition supports historical antigen status. Contemporary locus identity and missing matched expression measurements remain unresolved; a related BAGE paralog cannot be substituted.
